summary: This NREL web page describes the U.S. Life Cycle Inventory (USLCI) Database, created by NREL and partners to help life cycle assessment practitioners answer environmental impact questions. It explains the database's gate-to-gate, cradle-to-gate, and cradle-to-grave accounting of U.S. material and energy flows, its project goals, and the Federal Life Cycle Assessment Commons (FLCAC) interagency collaboration. It also lists resources, citation guidance, and a contact.
one_line: NREL's U.S. Life Cycle Inventory Database and the Federal LCA Commons, a federal effort to provide critically reviewed LCA data.
key_facts: NREL and its partners created the U.S. Life Cycle Inventory (USLCI) Database to help life cycle assessment practitioners answer questions about environmental impact.

The USLCI database provides gate-to-gate, cradle-to-gate, and cradle-to-grave accounting of energy and material flows into and out of the environment for producing a material, component, or assembly in the U.S.
A goal of the USLCI Database project is to maintain data quality and transparency.
A goal of the USLCI Database project is to cover commonly used U.S. materials, products, and processes with up-to-date, critically reviewed life cycle inventory data.
A goal of the USLCI Database project is to maintain compatibility with international life cycle inventory databases.
The Federal Life Cycle Assessment Commons (FLCAC) is an interagency community of practice for life cycle assessment research methods.
The FLCAC has been formalized through a memorandum of understanding between the United States Department of Agriculture, Department of Energy, and Environmental Protection Agency.
The FLCAC aims to make federal data sets freely available through a web-based data repository.
The USLCI database supports data submission and end-use through resources hosted on GitHub, including a Data Submission Handbook, Database Archives, a Release Change Log, and an Update Press Release.
NREL published a Quick Help Series of video tutorials on how to use the database.
The page suggests referencing the database as "U.S. Life Cycle Inventory Database." (2012), National Renewable Energy Laboratory, 2012.
Questions about the USLCI can be sent to lci@nrel.gov.
Alberta Carpenter is listed as an Environmental Engineer, Life Cycle Analysis at NREL.
The National Renewable Energy Laboratory is a national laboratory of the U.S. Department of Energy, operated by the Alliance for Sustainable Energy LLC.
